Currently · Poda

What I own
at Poda.

Not a single-lane design role. Brand, ecommerce, CRM, marketplace, social and copy, one voice, kept consistent across every channel a customer meets Poda in.

N°01: Brand & Creative Direction

An editorial, not a wellness brand

Defined Poda's visual world as candid, flash-heavy and slightly chaotic, a goth/alt bar universe over sterile wellness branding, built on references to Graza, Grüns, Drumroll and Haru Foods without copying any of them.

N°02: Shopify & Ecommerce

Designed, built, shipped

Homepage and landing pages built directly in Liquid, HTML, CSS and JS (heroes, comparisons, FAQs, creator content), keeping the matcha-smear canvas animation alive without wrecking mobile load times.

N°03: Conversion (CRO)

Designed against real objections

Pages rebuilt around what actually stops a sale (price, prep time, bitterness, clumping, coffee dependence), with performance data deciding what shipped, not opinion.

N°04: CRM & Email

Klaviyo, end to end

Owns welcome, post-purchase, abandoned-cart and subscriber flows: strategy, copy, HTML build and the performance read that shapes the next send.

N°05: Amazon Marketplace

Listing, A+, storefront

Full image set, A+ Content and Storefront built around one-line hooks like “coffee could never,” plus the compliance-safe hero variants Amazon actually requires.

N°06: Social & Content

Formats built to recur

Recurring series built around real people's relationship with matcha, not just the tube, including a Reels series currently in post, Matcha People.

N°07: Copy & Positioning

Every line, rewritten

Site, Amazon, email and captions rewritten until they stopped sounding corporate, generic, or AI-flavored, and started sounding like Poda.

Also directing · @drinkpoda Matcha People: an ongoing series retelling real people's stories, mostly Angelenos, through AI-generated stop-motion visuals and voiceover. Scripted and directed start to finish, open-ended rather than a fixed episode count. None released yet.

About

I'm a Lahore-based creative working end to end on how a DTC brand actually reaches someone, from the first Reel, through the Shopify checkout and the Amazon listing, to the email that brings them back. A psychology background underneath all of it: three years studying why people actually behave the way they do, now spent on why they actually buy.
